newsitem.title: USA: FAA says Fine pilot suspension not due to crash. [CORRECTED 08:45 GMT 9/8]
newsitem.headline: FAA says Fine pilot suspension not due to crash. [CORRECTED 08:45 GMT 9/8]

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration said Friday it had proposed in June and July to suspend the flying certificates of 29 pilots employed by Fine Air Services Inc, an action unrelated to Thursday's crash of a Fine Air DC-8-61F in Miami, an FAA statement indicated.
(FAA corrects to show it proposed the suspension in June and July.)
"The proposed suspensions are based on evidence that the pilots exceeded maximum limitations for DC-8 operations into two airports in South America," an FAA statement said.
"The evidence is related to the pressure altitude of the high altitude airports at the time the operations took place," the statement said.

The FAA said it could provide no further information about the case because they are still pending (corrects from "The FAA said it had no further information about the incidents but the cases remained open"). The proposed suspension would last 60 to 90 days. FAA spokeswoman Kathleen Bergen said the action was not final or immediate and would follow due process procedures.

The FAA also said Friday it had separately undertaken a routine national inspection of Fine Air carried out from March 31 to April 18. The inspection "identified issues for further investigations in the areas of flight operations training, maintenance manuals and weight and balance," the FAA said.
Bergen said the FAA issued the statement Friday about the two separate issues because it had received media inquiries about in the wake of the Fine Air crash in Miami.
"We would not normally issue a press release regarding action we propose against pilots. There are privacy considerations," Bergen said.
